sessions.title: Lunch

In this session, we will describe the architecture and features of a client-side AI-based agent that helps diagnose and remediate common issues faced by our customers.

sessions.title: Implementing Microsoft Entra Private Access for 1000+ Users: A Real-World Journey (intro)
sessions.description:
Discover how Microsoft Entra Private Access revolutionizes secure access to private corporate resources by eliminating traditional VPN complexities with a modern Zero Trust approach. In this session, we will explore:

What is Microsoft Entra Private Access?

Learn the fundamentals of Microsoft’s cloud-delivered secure access solution, its key features such as identity-centric controls, conditional access, multi-factor authentication, and per-app adaptive access that provide seamless and secure connectivity for remote and on-premises users across hybrid environments.

How to Implement Microsoft Entra Private Access at Scale Dive into a practical, real-world case study of deploying Entra Private Access in an enterprise with more than 1,000 users. Understand step-by-step how to configure enterprise applications, set up connectors, apply granular access policies, and roll out secure access without disrupting user productivity.

Lessons Learned and Best Practices Gain invaluable insights from the implementation journey, including challenges encountered, strategies for effective segmentation and policy enforcement, user adoption tips, and integration with existing Microsoft 365 security frameworks to maximize security and usability.

Whether you are planning to modernize your network access strategy or looking for proven solutions to secure your private applications, this session will provide a comprehensive roadmap and actionable takeaways to empower your organization’s Zero Trust journey with Microsoft Entra Private Access.

sessions.title: The Next Wave of AVD and Windows 365 Adoption (intro)
sessions.description:
21 years in End User Computing, and I watched the first AVD and Windows 365 deployments stick to the easy jobs.

Call centres. Task workers. Lightly managed desktops.

Knowledge workers are a different problem. More apps, more dependencies, more user state, and far less tolerance for a slow login.

This session covers what changes when you scale AVD and Windows 365 to that population:

Application delivery and management without rebuilding images every time something changes User onboarding and profile management at scale Visibility into performance and user experience across the environment The operational blockers that stall large deployments, and how people are getting past them We'll also look at where the platform and the ecosystem around it are heading, and what that means for your next rollout.

And while everyone is talking about AI, we’ll introduce our own interpretation: AppVentiX Inside.

We’ll revisit what we showed last year, demonstrate how your feedback shaped the product, and dive into the latest capabilities with real-world examples and live demos. Expect less slides, more tech, and a practical look at consistent workspace management and application control across your hybrid Windows estate.

sessions.title: EUC for the Agentic Enterprise - The Workspace as a Secure Execution Layer for Agentic AI (intro)
sessions.description:
Enterprises spent years and significant capital building sophisticated EUC and VDI estates. As remote-work patterns normalized, SaaS adoption accelerated, renewal pressures increased, and alternative application and desktop delivery models matured, many organizations began to reassess the long-term strategic role of those environments.

Agentic AI should force organizations to reassess the value of their existing EUC platforms and the role those platforms can play in the controlled integration of autonomous agents into the enterprise.

This does not remove the need to modernize authentication, migrate appropriate services out of legacy data centers, improve data governance, or address technical debt. In fact, agentic AI makes those modernization efforts more important. But many of the architectural and operational principles required to run EUC well controlled execution, identity-based access, application entitlement, isolation, policy enforcement, observability, lifecycle management, and operational accountability closely resemble the disciplines enterprises will need when introducing autonomous software.

At the same time, the EUC ecosystem itself is evolving. Agent identities, managed execution environments, Conditional Access for agents, MCP gateways, Cloud PCs for agents, and AI-specific policy controls are beginning to blur the line between the traditional user workspace and a governed execution environment for software actors.

This session explores whether mature EUC architecture can provide a practical starting point for secure agentic AI adoption. We will examine what translates well, what does not, and what still needs to be modernized before agents can be introduced safely at enterprise scale.

Attendees will leave with an understanding of how agentic AI changes familiar EUC assumptions around identity, execution, applications, data, and trust. The session will explore how established EUC design principles may translate into agent governance; where Citrix, Windows 365, AVD, Horizon, and similar platforms could play a role as controlled execution environments; why legacy applications may keep EUC relevant in an agentic world; and what still has to change across authentication, data governance, DLP, observability, lifecycle management, and cloud architecture.

None of it goes through Studio.

sessions.title: Stop Giving AI Agents Your Desktop (intro session)
sessions.description: The dominant CUA architecture — agent -> VM -> screenshot -> mouse — treats the agent as a very fast remote employee. But remote computing spent three decades building the primitives agents actually need: session brokering, isolation, process and window ownership, input routing, graphics capture, auditing, and human shadowing. This talk reframes MCP as the control plane over session infrastructure, not the runtime itself. Drawing on lessons from building Vedon, an experimental desktop execution stack for computer-use agents, I'll cover multi-session orchestration, browser attachment, agent/human coexistence, and why VDI-style infrastructure — far from being obsolete — may become the substrate agents run on.

sessions.title: Architecting Sovereign DaaS: Transforming Legacy VDI -> Cloud-Native Private Cloud VDI Platform
sessions.description: This 30-minute session outlines an enterprise architecture blueprint for transforming an established on-premises Citrix estate into a sovereign, automated Desktop-as-a-Service (DaaS) model inside a private cloud. We examine the architectural decoupling of the control plane from the workload execution layer, enabling zero-touch lifecycle management, automated image pipelines (BYOI), and standardized T-shirt sizing through ITSM self-service integration. Furthermore, the presentation walks through a phased migration roadmap that balances operational continuity with multi-stack resilience across private data centers, while highlighting strategic trigger points for market evaluations and vendor-agnostic portability.

sessions.title: Compliant on Paper, Wild West in Practice: Getting EUC Ready for AI with a little OI
sessions.description:
The architecture looks sound. The policies are documented. Day to day, application sprawl, accumulated privileges and years of exceptions tell a different story. What happens when user-facing AI - and eventually autonomous agents – inherits (hopefully, not exploits) that environment?

Drawing on experience across large government, healthcare and financial organizations, this session examines the gap between formal controls and operational reality. We’ll explore how organizational inefficiencies, competing priorities and politics allow workarounds to become permanent dependencies, leaving users and endpoints less ready for AI than the diagrams suggest.

Getting ready starts with the basics: knowing what’s running, who owns it, what it can access and how those boundaries are enforced. We’ll discuss practical steps toward bringing existing EUC environments into line with their intended controls, including sound identity and privilege management, application governance and endpoint discipline, before AI compounds the flaws already there.

He believes getting ready for AI starts with putting OI (Organic Intelligence) to work.

sessions.title: How We Escaped a 12K Seat EUC Renewal in 6 Months (PART 2)
sessions.description: Soaring renewal quotes. Multi-year lock-ins. “All-you-can-eat” licences that leave a bitter aftertaste. When private-equity-owned EUC vendors rewrite the rules, your IT budget can quickly become their growth strategy. This is the real-world story of a 12k-seat renewal that became a six-month migration race. Learn how we HDeXited, what we replaced it with, and the practical decisions, trade-offs, and lessons that got us out.

speakers.name: Neil Spellings
speakers.bio:
Neil has spent more than 20 years convincing large organisations that desktops do not necessarily need to live under desks. He has worked with Citrix since the WinFrame and MetaFrame days, which makes him old enough to remember when “the cloud” was mainly a weather-related availability risk. A ex-Citrix Technology Professional since 2013 and a TOGAF-certified Enterprise Architect, and more recently a Microsoft MVP, Neil has accumulated enough acronyms to make a network diagram look concise. He has contributed to Citrix certification exams, delivered large XenApp environments, and has strong opinions on virtualisation, EUC, cloud platforms, automation, and why “it worked in test” is not an operational strategy. sessions.title: Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) - A new encryption era till 2030?

Why do we need that and what’s the law regulators for the next years? Learn why every SSL 443 offloaded service is affected by PQC and what „Harvest Now, Decrypt Later“ means.

In this Session, I will share my learnings from the field, migrating financial and government environments as early adopters to PQC (Hybrid and Force-Mode) and what that means for TLS Handshake-Performance (Packet CPU, Crypto Hardware Offloading,…) - doesn’t matter on which ADC or LoadBalancer solution you’re on. sessions.title: Confidence, Not Dashboards: What Genealogy Taught Me About AI Observability
sessions.description: When I started tracing my family tree, an online record confidently placed my great-grandmother in Bad Langensalza. The primary sources said Bad Homburg. A trusted-looking source had hallucinated - and untangling it took archives, church books, and a lot of cross-checking to decide which claim deserved confidence. That is exactly the discipline AI observability demands. As AI grows from autocomplete into agents that act on our behalf, "the model said so" is no longer a source. We need provenance - where did this answer come from? We need confidence - how sure are we, and what would change our mind? We need negative results - what did we rule out, and why? In this session I'll use a real family mystery as the narrative spine and map every genealogy method - citing primary sources, rating confidence, disproving false positives, respecting data-access rules - onto the AI observability toolkit you'll need in production. You'll leave seeing observability not as another dashboard, but as the practice of knowing how much to trust each claim your system makes. No Kirchenbuch required - just the question genealogists have asked for centuries: where does that come from? TBA

sessions.title: EUC for the Agentic Enterprise - Workspace as a Secure Execution Layer for Agentic AI (PART 2)
sessions.description:
Enterprises spent years and significant capital building sophisticated EUC and VDI estates. As remote-work patterns normalized, SaaS adoption accelerated, renewal pressures increased, and alternative application and desktop delivery models matured, many organizations began to reassess the long-term strategic role of those environments.

Agentic AI should force organizations to reassess the value of their existing EUC platforms and the role those platforms can play in the controlled integration of autonomous agents into the enterprise.

This does not remove the need to modernize authentication, migrate appropriate services out of legacy data centers, improve data governance, or address technical debt. In fact, agentic AI makes those modernization efforts more important. But many of the architectural and operational principles required to run EUC well controlled execution, identity-based access, application entitlement, isolation, policy enforcement, observability, lifecycle management, and operational accountability closely resemble the disciplines enterprises will need when introducing autonomous software.

At the same time, the EUC ecosystem itself is evolving. Agent identities, managed execution environments, Conditional Access for agents, MCP gateways, Cloud PCs for agents, and AI-specific policy controls are beginning to blur the line between the traditional user workspace and a governed execution environment for software actors.

This session explores whether mature EUC architecture can provide a practical starting point for secure agentic AI adoption. We will examine what translates well, what does not, and what still needs to be modernized before agents can be introduced safely at enterprise scale.

Attendees will leave with an understanding of how agentic AI changes familiar EUC assumptions around identity, execution, applications, data, and trust. The session will explore how established EUC design principles may translate into agent governance; where Citrix, Windows 365, AVD, Horizon, and similar platforms could play a role as controlled execution environments; why legacy applications may keep EUC relevant in an agentic world; and what still has to change across authentication, data governance, DLP, observability, lifecycle management, and cloud architecture.

sessions.title: Inside Device & App Redirection: How Remoting Protocols Move the World Across the Wire
sessions.description:
A deep technical tour of how remoting protocols shuttle devices, applications, and media streams between endpoints. We’ll compare redirection models for USB, printers, audio, webcams, file systems, clipboards, COM automation, graphics, and app virtualization.The dominant CUA architecture — agent -> VM -> screenshot -> mouse — treats the agent as a very fast remote employee. But remote computing spent three decades building the primitives agents actually need: session brokering, isolation, process and window ownership, input routing, graphics capture, auditing, and human shadowing. This talk reframes MCP as the control plane over session infrastructure, not the runtime itself. Drawing on lessons from building Vedon, an experimental desktop execution stack for computer-use agents, I'll cover multi-session orchestration, browser attachment, agent/human coexistence, and why VDI-style infrastructure — far from being obsolete — may become the substrate agents run Denis Gundarev has over 25 years of experience in EUC, VDI, remote computing, and desktop operating systems, with a background spanning Citrix, VMware, AWS, and Microsoft.

featuredSponsors.name: Auxilium IT
featuredSponsors.text: With a focus on building enduring business relationships with vendors and clients, Auxilium IT Consultancy excel in EUC consulting across diverse industry sectors within the enterprise. Additionally, we leverage our expertise to provide tailored managed services that cater specifically to SMB clients throughout the United Kingdom, bringing together vendors and clients to deliver exceptional value.

featuredSponsors.name: AppVentiX
featuredSponsors.text: AppVentiX is a modern application delivery and workspace management platform built for enterprise environments. Designed as a seamless replacement for Microsoft App-V infrastructure, AppVentiX enables organizations to continue delivering existing App-V packages while simultaneously supporting MSIX and traditional applications from a single platform. Beyond application delivery, AppVentiX Workspace Control provides granular user environment management, dynamic configuration based on context, user personalization, and integrated Microsoft App Control policy management. Whether you’re managing physical desktops, AVD, Citrix, Omnissa, RDS, or hybrid environments, AppVentiX helps reduce complexity, eliminate legacy infrastructure dependencies, and gives administrators precise control over applications, policies, and the end-user workspace.

featuredSponsors.name: EUC Score
featuredSponsors.text: EUC Score by Dr. Benny Tritsch IT Consulting. Your Ultimate Guide to EUC Performance Tests and Digital Employee Experience (DEX) Analysis. Measuring perceived remote end-user experience in an organized, valid and repeatable way.

panel.name: Eugene Kalayev
panel.bio:
Eugene is ControlUp old-timer, deeply involved in planning and executing the product's technological vision. His areas of expertise include virtualization, cloud computing, Windows Server, PowerShell, VDI. Eugene has extensive experience in training IT professionals, and holds various industry certifications from Microsoft, Citrix, Cisco, Splunk and the Scrum Alliance, as well as a Master's degree in Social and Organizational Psychology.

LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com /in/ eugenekalayev

panel.name: Kristin Brown
panel.bio: Kristin has 20 years of tech industry experience across sales, partner management, product management, marketing, and leadership roles. She has developed domain expertise in printing, enterprise mobility management, digital experience creation, and eCommerce. At Go Autonomous, the leader in Autonomous Commerce for B2B organizations, she leads the global partner ecosystem strategy and program. She is passionate about innovative technologies, including AI, and how they drive efficiency and growth.

panel.name: Chris Twiest
panel.bio: Chris Twiest is the Solution Innovation Manager at ControlUp, where he leads the Innovation Guild — a cross-functional initiative focused on developing creative solutions for real-world customer challenges. With two decades of experience in managing, creating, and automating workspace environments, Chris combines deep technical expertise with a passion for building practical, scalable tools. In his role, he drives innovation across ControlUp’s platform by designing and prototyping new features, building in-product script libraries, and collaborating closely with customers, product managers, and the community. Chris is also a frequent blogger, speaker, and advocate for turning complex problems into streamlined workflows.

panel.name: Netanel Ofri
panel.bio: Netanel has worked as an Engineering Manager for ControlUp since 2022, and prior to that as a Full-Stack Developer since 2015. Netanel's primary responsibility is developing The ControlUp DEX AI chat assistant.

panel.name: Samuel Legrand
panel.bio:
Sam is Field CTO International at ControlUp, covering everything outside the Americas. Over 8 years at the company, he's moved from Presales in South EMEA into a role spanning deal support, competitive strategy, and partner enablement, always with a hands-on approach to the platform itself.

Based in Marbella, Spain, Sam is French-speaking and gets by just fine in Spanish. He loves traveling and discovering new places, with a growing list of destinations still to tick off. Outside of work, he's kept on his toes by his daughter Erika, who tends to be right more often than he'd like to admit.

panel.name: Jason Samuel
panel.bio:
Jason is a longtime member of the end-user computing community, technologist, advisor, and speaker with nearly three decades of experience across EUC, virtualization, cloud, automation, and security.

Over the years, he has been recognized through several industry and community programs, including Citrix Technology Professional (CTP), VMware vExpert and EUC Champion, among others. Jason has worked with hundreds of enterprises around the world and has shared his experience at industry and community events across five continents.

Throughout his career, Jason has remained closely involved with the EUC community, sharing practical experience and perspectives gained from working with customers, partners, and technology teams around the world. Today, he is also a product leader at Citrix, bringing both practitioner and product perspectives to the technologies he has spent much of his career working with.

panel.name: Alex Cooper
panel.bio: Alex is the spiritual organizer of PubForum, E2EMVC, E2EMVC and what ever other names will follow. Alex has been Microsoft, Citrix, VMware and Netware instructor, trainer and architect for over 30 years and helped many thousand professionals around the globe to get their Mainframe, SBC, EUC knowledge up to speed. As well as helping many small, midsize and big multinational companies to architect, design and implement digital user experience, virtualization and cloud solutions.

panel.name: James O'Regan
panel.bio:
James is a Product Marketing Manager and Community Lead at Liquidware, bringing 21 years of End User Computing (EUC) experience across the realities of desktops, VDI, and the day-to-day grind of keeping users productive.

He combines deep technical credibility with commercial storytelling: turning complex EUC challenges into clear messaging that resonates with IT teams, leaders, and partners.

He is active in the wider EUC community, regularly collaborating with peers across the industry and speaking at events such as E2EVC.

In February 2024, James and Gerjon Kunst launched an AI podcast: The Impact of AI: Explored. The goal is simple: cut through the hype, translate what’s real into plain language, and help IT and EUC professionals make better decisions about AI based on practical experience, not vendor noise.

panel.name: Andrew Morgan
panel.bio: Andrew came to AWS in 2019 from a large datacenter environment where he specialized VMware, Cisco UCS, and automation. His AWS career began on the Windows team in Premium Support. By 2020, he was the Lead Subject Matter Expert on Amazon WorkSpaces. He then transitioned to a Solutions Architecture role specializing in End User Computing (EUC). Through his work on EUC services, he developed a passion for the DCV streaming protocol. In 2022, he started his current role as the DCV Developer Advocate.

panel.name: Denis Gundarev
panel.bio:
Denis has over 25 years of experience in EUC, VDI, remote computing, and desktop operating systems, with a background spanning Citrix, VMware, AWS, and Microsoft.

His work focuses on remoting protocols, session infrastructure, graphics, SDKs, and computer-use agents, especially making desktop environments reliable for both humans and AI.

panel.name: Douglas Brown
panel.bio: Douglas is the Vice President of Community at ControlUp responsible for energizing ControlUp's partners and partners through building and growing the new ControlUp Community. Before ControlUp, Douglas Brown was the Vice President of Community at IGEL Technology. Mr. Brown built and grew the IGEL Community from zero to 9,000 members and 330,000 messages posted, making it the most active community in End-User Computing. Douglas was also responsible for the IGEL VIP Program, managing over 45 IGEL experts and visionaries. He has headed up the Technical Publications team with the goal is better organizing and prioritizing quality content. Prior, Douglas was the Global Technology Evangelist, traveling the world to share the IGEL story. Mr. Brown was the Founder of DABCC, Inc. Doug has more than 25 years of experience in virtualization, cloud, and end-user computing technologies and markets. DABCC is the first and most visited website dedicated to all elements of the end-user computing. Industry. Prior to DABCC, Doug worked at Citrix Systems, Inc. as a Senior Systems Engineer from 2001 to 2004, where he developed the leading Citrix deployment system, "Methodology in a Box," which has more than a million downloads. Additionally, his peers and management at Citrix named Doug Systems Engineer of the Year in 2002. From 2005 to 2016, Doug was awarded the Microsoft Most Valuable Professional (MVP) by Microsoft Corporation for his contributions to the industry. He has also been acknowledged with the Citrix Technology Professional (CTP) and VMware vEXPERT awards for his continued support in the IT community. Doug speaks at leading industry events and has been a prolific author over the past 20 years.

panel.name: Michael Shuster
panel.bio: Michael is CEO of Ferroque Systems, where his team helps organizations modernize complex IT environments while continuing his lifelong battle against scope creep, vendor nonsense, and his own inbox. Equal parts technologist, strategist, and professionally overcommitted raccoon, he brings deep expertise and the unsettling confidence of someone who has read too many enterprise architecture documents and seriously believes he is important.
